settings.question: How many ratti is 1 carat?
settings.answer: 1 carat equals approximately 1.09 ratti. This is because 1 carat weighs 200 milligrams while 1 ratti weighs 182 milligrams (200 ÷ 182 ≈ 1.0989).

settings.question: How do I convert ratti to carat?
settings.answer: Multiply the ratti value by 0.91. For example, a 5-ratti gemstone weighs 5 × 0.91 = 4.55 carats. You can also simply type the ratti value into the converter above.

settings.question: Why do astrologers prescribe gemstones in ratti?
settings.answer: Ratti is the traditional Indian unit used in Vedic astrology for centuries. Astrological texts and practitioners specify minimum gemstone weights in ratti, while modern gem certification labs weigh stones in carats — which is why this conversion is essential when buying an astrological gemstone.

settings.question: Is pakki ratti different from kachi ratti?
settings.answer: Yes. Pakki (standard) ratti is the fixed modern value of 182 mg used by jewellers and this converter. Kachi ratti refers to the traditional practice of weighing against actual ratti (gunja) seeds, which varies between roughly 100–120 mg. Always confirm which measure is being used — reputable sellers use pakki ratti.

settings.question: How many ratti are there in 1 gram?
settings.answer: 1 gram equals approximately 5.49 ratti (1000 mg ÷ 182 mg). It also equals exactly 5 carats.
